مُعَضَّدٌ (tropical:) A garment having some figured, or embroidered, work on the place of the عَضُد [or upper arm] (S, O, K) of its wearer: (S, O:) or marked with stripes in the form of the عَضُد: (TA:) or of which its figured work is in its sides: (Lh, TA:) or i. q. مُضَلَّعٌ [q. v.]. (A, TA.) ―
-b2- إِبِلٌ مُعَضَّدَةٌ Camels branded upon the عَضُد [or arm] with the mark called عِضَاد. (S, O, L.) ―
-b3- In a description of the Prophet, as related by Yahyà Ibn-Ma'een, the epithet مُعَضَّدٌ is applied to him, meaning Firmly made: but accord. to the relation commonly retained in the memory, it is مُقَصَّد [q. v.]. (TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
